I've always been an introverted person. I've never been great with people, which has always bothered me.

In high school, I tried to break out of my shell and connect with people. I made friends, opened my heart to others, and all that other high school stuff. What it got me was depression. When I started connecting with people, I was confronted with their pain, and I couldn't handle it on top of my own problems. Due to my disposition, I tried to help, anyway. In the end, I was on a dangerous precipice, and I cut myself off from everyone. I stopped talking to a lot of people and moved away. I needed some time to figure things out and come to terms with myself.

Over the next year, I only stayed in contact with a few people from home. I didn't try to make any connections with people in my new home because I didn't think I was ready, and I didn't know where I would be in the coming months. I took a year to center myself, and I ended up moving back from where I'd come.

I'd only stayed in touch with a few people, but they were good friends. I tried to branch out from there, but it was harder than I remembered, and things were different than they were in high school. In the process of trying to reconnect with people, I got burned again. I ended up withdrawing. In combination with other events over the past year, my few friendships became strained and distant. I had no one to help me with my pain, so I ignored it and told myself that I was happier without other people. Any time I connected with another person, we woild hurt each other. Every time, I'd end up on that same ledge. I didn't want to put myself in that situation anymore.

But, recently, I've had a lot of things stressing me out, and it all piled up until I was in the emergency room one morning because I had become so anxious that I convinced myself I was about to die. During this time, I realized that I had very few people beyond my direct family to help me through situations, like these. This is something I had been trying not to confront this whole time. In that instant, I had to come face-to-face with the fact that I was nearly alone.

I thought that I was stronger through isolation. I thought that I was protecting myself from closing myself off to others. I thought that I wouldn't get hurt if no one could get to me. However, I can't ignore the fact that I need other poeple, sometimes, and I've put myself in a situation where I don't have a safety net for those times.

This may just be me making excuses, but I don't know how to talk to people any longer. I'm afraid. Both of what's inside of them, as well as what's inside of me. I've been hurt and hurt others in the past, and it only brings me to bad places. I don't know what direction to go from here...
I cut myself off from people, and now I don't know if I made the right choice...
